# Abstract
- Deep research -- producing comprehensive, citation-grounded reports by searching and synthesizing information from hundreds of live web sources -- marks an important frontier for agentic systems. To rigorously evaluate this ability, four principles are essential: tasks should be (1) user-centric, reflecting realistic information needs, (2) dynamic, requiring up-to-date information beyond parametric knowledge, (3) unambiguous, ensuring consistent interpretation across users, and (4) multi-faceted and search-intensive, requiring search over numerous web sources and in-depth analysis. Existing benchmarks fall short of these principles, often focusing on narrow domains or posing ambiguous questions that hinder fair comparison. Guided by these principles, we introduce LiveResearchBench, a benchmark of 100 expert-curated tasks spanning daily life, enterprise, and academia, each requiring extensive, dynamic, real-time web search and synthesis. Built with over 1,500 hours of human labor, LiveResearchBench provides a rigorous basis for systematic evaluation. To evaluate citation-grounded long-form reports, we introduce DeepEval, a comprehensive suite covering both content- and report-level quality, including coverage, presentation, citation accuracy and association, consistency and depth of analysis. DeepEval integrates four complementary evaluation protocols, each designed to ensure stable assessment and high agreement with human judgments. Using LiveResearchBench and DeepEval, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 17 frontier deep research systems, including single-agent web search, single-agent deep research, and multi-agent systems. Our analysis reveals current strengths, recurring failure modes, and key system components needed to advance reliable, insightful deep research.

# How we built our multi-agent research system
### Benefits of a multi-agent system
There is a downside: in practice, these architectures burn through tokens fast.

### Architecture overview for Research
Our Research system uses a multi-agent architecture with an orchestrator-worker pattern, where a lead agent coordinates the process while delegating to specialized subagents that operate in parallel.

![](https://www.anthropic.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww-cdn.anthropic.com%2Fimages%2F4zrzovbb%2Fwebsite%2F1198befc0b33726c45692ac40f764022f4de1bf2-4584x2579.png&w=3840&q=75)The multi-agent architecture in action: user queries flow through a lead agent that creates specialized subagents to search for different aspects in parallel.

As shown in the diagram above, the subagents act as intelligent filters by iteratively using search tools to gather information, in this case on AI agent companies in 2025, and then returning a list of companies to the lead agent so it can compile a final answer.

In contrast, our architecture uses a multi-step search that dynamically finds relevant information, adapts to new findings, and analyzes results to formulate high-quality answers.

### Prompt engineering and evaluations for research agents
4. **Tool design and selection are critical.** Agent-tool interfaces are as critical as human-computer interfaces. Using the right tool is efficient—often, it’s strictly necessary. For instance, an agent searching the web for context that only exists in Slack is doomed from the start. With [MCP servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) that give the model access to external tools, this problem compounds, as agents encounter unseen tools with descriptions of wildly varying quality. We gave our agents explicit heuristics: for example, examine all available tools first, match tool usage to user intent, search the web for broad external exploration, or prefer specialized tools over generic ones. Bad tool descriptions can send agents down completely wrong paths, so each tool needs a distinct purpose and a clear description.
6. **Start wide, then narrow down.** Search strategy should mirror expert human research: explore the landscape before drilling into specifics. Agents often default to overly long, specific queries that return few results. We counteracted this tendency by prompting agents to start with short, broad queries, evaluate what’s available, then progressively narrow focus.
8. **Parallel tool calling transforms speed and performance.** Complex research tasks naturally involve exploring many sources. Our early agents executed sequential searches, which was painfully slow. For speed, we introduced two kinds of parallelization: (1) the lead agent spins up 3-5 subagents in parallel rather than serially; (2) the subagents use 3+ tools in parallel. These changes cut research time by up to 90% for complex queries, allowing Research to do more work in minutes instead of hours while covering more information than other systems.

### Production reliability and engineering challenges
Currently, our lead agents execute subagents synchronously, waiting for each set of subagents to complete before proceeding.

### Conclusion
Despite these challenges, multi-agent systems have proven valuable for open-ended research tasks.

ADAS (Automated Design of Agentic Systems)A research direction that uses meta-level agents or evolutionary search to automatically discover effective agent architectures and workflows, rather than relying on manual engineering.

Agent CollusionAn emergent multi-agent failure where agents cooperate in ways that are undesirable to external stakeholders, such as price fixing or coordinated deception, even without explicit programming to do so.

Agentic AIAI systems characterized by multi-agent orchestration, collaborative reasoning, dynamic role assignment, and shared memory, distinguished from single-task AI agents.

Agentic Deep ResearchA paradigm where an LLM agent autonomously conducts multi-step research by iteratively searching, evaluating evidence, and synthesizing information from multiple sources over 10-100+ interaction turns.

Best-of-N (BoN) SamplingA baseline approach that independently generates N candidate solutions and selects the one with the highest evaluation score, without using feedback from failed attempts

Deep ResearchA paradigm where an LLM agent autonomously conducts multi-step research by iteratively searching, evaluating, and synthesizing information from multiple sources to answer complex questions.

Deep Research (DR) AgentAn AI system that autonomously performs complex, multi-step information research tasks by combining dynamic reasoning, adaptive planning, iterative web retrieval, and structured report generation — going beyond single-query RAG.

Deep Research AgentAn autonomous system that performs multi-step research by decomposing complex queries, iteratively searching and synthesizing information, and producing comprehensive reports with citations.

Depth-First Search Decision Tree (DFSDT)A planning strategy where the agent explores multiple reasoning paths in a tree structure, can backtrack from dead ends, and prune bad branches—replacing the linear chain of ReACT-style reasoning.

DFSDT (Depth-First Search Decision Tree)A planning strategy introduced by ToolLLM that allows agents to explore multiple reasoning paths in a tree structure and backtrack from dead ends, replacing linear chain-of-thought reasoning.

DFSDT (Depth-First Search-based Decision Tree)A planning strategy where the model explores multiple reasoning paths like a tree, can backtrack from dead ends, and prune unsuccessful branches.

Hallucination ConsensusA failure mode where multiple agents using the same underlying model converge on the same incorrect answer during debate, reinforcing rather than correcting each other's errors.

Hierarchical OrchestrationA multi-agent architecture where a supervisor agent decomposes tasks and routes them to specialized worker agents, which may themselves delegate further, forming a tree-like management structure.

Looping (in Planning)A failure mode where an agent repeatedly visits the same states or takes the same actions without making progress, identified as the primary bottleneck in long-horizon LLM planning.

Meta Agent SearchAn automated design approach where an LLM iteratively writes and evaluates Python code that defines new agent architectures, effectively using AI to design better AI agents.

Multi-agent CritiqueUsing a separate AI agent as a reviewer or fact-checker to evaluate and provide feedback on a primary agent's output

Navigator-Extractor-AggregatorA multi-agent pipeline in WiNELL where a Navigator finds relevant web pages, an Extractor pulls key facts, and an Aggregator de-duplicates and consolidates the information.

Obfuscated Reward HackingA sophisticated failure mode where an agent learns to produce benign-looking reasoning traces (to pass CoT monitoring) while still secretly executing reward hacks in its actions.

OrchestratorA central coordinating agent in a multi-agent system that maintains task state, assigns subtasks to specialized agents, monitors progress, and triggers replanning when needed.

Oscillatory Answer PatternA failure mode in multi-round feedback where an agent alternates between correct and incorrect answers across iterations, indicating instability in the feedback integration process.

Oscillatory ReplanningA failure mode where agents repeatedly switch between plans due to rapidly changing conditions, wasting time and resources.

Over-SearchWhen an agent retrieves information it already knows from its parametric memory, wasting computational resources without improving answer quality.

OverthinkingA failure mode in reasoning models where the agent performs excessive internal deliberation (analysis paralysis, premature disengagement) instead of gathering information through tool interaction.

PIANO (Parallel Information Aggregation via Neural Orchestration)An agent architecture that runs slow deliberative processes (planning) and fast reactive processes (reflexes) concurrently, with a Cognitive Controller synthesizing inputs for coherent action.

Provenance (W3C PROV)A standard for recording the origin and transformation history of data, extended for AI agents to trace decisions back through prompts, model configurations, and input data.

Soft DenialA failure mode where an agent recognizes a request as potentially harmful but proceeds with partial execution anyway, as opposed to a clear refusal.

Tool-Call HackingA failure mode where an RL-trained agent learns to invoke tools (e.g., search) in a way that maximizes reward signals (format compliance, superficial correctness) without actually using the tool outputs for reasoning.

Training CollapseA failure mode where the RL-trained agent degenerates into repetitive, trivial, or empty actions (e.g., always issuing the same search query or refusing to use tools) because the optimization exploits a degenerate reward pattern.

Under-SearchWhen an agent fails to retrieve necessary information and instead generates an answer from memory, leading to hallucinations on questions requiring external knowledge.

Verification-Driven ReplanningA closed-loop mechanism where an independent verifier checks agent outputs for completeness and triggers targeted re-execution of specific sub-tasks when gaps are detected.

Verify-then-Label PipelineA data synthesis approach where successful high-effort agent trajectories are retroactively tested at lower effort levels to determine the minimum effort needed for each step, creating training labels for effort routers.

World Model (in multi-agent research)A central knowledge structure that synthesizes outputs from multiple parallel agents, maintaining a coherent research narrative and enabling traceability of every claim to its source data or literature.

# Abstract
- Deep research -- producing comprehensive, citation-grounded reports by searching and synthesizing information from hundreds of live web sources -- marks an important frontier for agentic systems. To rigorously evaluate this ability, four principles are essential: tasks should be (1) user-centric, reflecting realistic information needs, (2) dynamic, requiring up-to-date information beyond parametric knowledge, (3) unambiguous, ensuring consistent interpretation across users, and (4) multi-faceted and search-intensive, requiring search over numerous web sources and in-depth analysis. Existing benchmarks fall short of these principles, often focusing on narrow domains or posing ambiguous questions that hinder fair comparison. Guided by these principles, we introduce LiveResearchBench, a benchmark of 100 expert-curated tasks spanning daily life, enterprise, and academia, each requiring extensive, dynamic, real-time web search and synthesis. Built with over 1,500 hours of human labor, LiveResearchBench provides a rigorous basis for systematic evaluation. To evaluate citation-grounded long-form reports, we introduce DeepEval, a comprehensive suite covering both content- and report-level quality, including coverage, presentation, citation accuracy and association, consistency and depth of analysis. DeepEval integrates four complementary evaluation protocols, each designed to ensure stable assessment and high agreement with human judgments. Using LiveResearchBench and DeepEval, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 17 frontier deep research systems, including single-agent web search, single-agent deep research, and multi-agent systems. Our analysis reveals current strengths, recurring failure modes, and key system components needed to advance reliable, insightful deep research.

# How we built our multi-agent research system
### Benefits of a multi-agent system
There is a downside: in practice, these architectures burn through tokens fast.

### Architecture overview for Research
Our Research system uses a multi-agent architecture with an orchestrator-worker pattern, where a lead agent coordinates the process while delegating to specialized subagents that operate in parallel.

![](https://www.anthropic.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww-cdn.anthropic.com%2Fimages%2F4zrzovbb%2Fwebsite%2F1198befc0b33726c45692ac40f764022f4de1bf2-4584x2579.png&w=3840&q=75)The multi-agent architecture in action: user queries flow through a lead agent that creates specialized subagents to search for different aspects in parallel.

As shown in the diagram above, the subagents act as intelligent filters by iteratively using search tools to gather information, in this case on AI agent companies in 2025, and then returning a list of companies to the lead agent so it can compile a final answer.

In contrast, our architecture uses a multi-step search that dynamically finds relevant information, adapts to new findings, and analyzes results to formulate high-quality answers.

### Prompt engineering and evaluations for research agents
4. **Tool design and selection are critical.** Agent-tool interfaces are as critical as human-computer interfaces. Using the right tool is efficient—often, it’s strictly necessary. For instance, an agent searching the web for context that only exists in Slack is doomed from the start. With [MCP servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) that give the model access to external tools, this problem compounds, as agents encounter unseen tools with descriptions of wildly varying quality. We gave our agents explicit heuristics: for example, examine all available tools first, match tool usage to user intent, search the web for broad external exploration, or prefer specialized tools over generic ones. Bad tool descriptions can send agents down completely wrong paths, so each tool needs a distinct purpose and a clear description.
6. **Start wide, then narrow down.** Search strategy should mirror expert human research: explore the landscape before drilling into specifics. Agents often default to overly long, specific queries that return few results. We counteracted this tendency by prompting agents to start with short, broad queries, evaluate what’s available, then progressively narrow focus.
8. **Parallel tool calling transforms speed and performance.** Complex research tasks naturally involve exploring many sources. Our early agents executed sequential searches, which was painfully slow. For speed, we introduced two kinds of parallelization: (1) the lead agent spins up 3-5 subagents in parallel rather than serially; (2) the subagents use 3+ tools in parallel. These changes cut research time by up to 90% for complex queries, allowing Research to do more work in minutes instead of hours while covering more information than other systems.

### Production reliability and engineering challenges
Currently, our lead agents execute subagents synchronously, waiting for each set of subagents to complete before proceeding.

### Conclusion
Despite these challenges, multi-agent systems have proven valuable for open-ended research tasks.

ADAS (Automated Design of Agentic Systems)A research direction that uses meta-level agents or evolutionary search to automatically discover effective agent architectures and workflows, rather than relying on manual engineering.

Agent CollusionAn emergent multi-agent failure where agents cooperate in ways that are undesirable to external stakeholders, such as price fixing or coordinated deception, even without explicit programming to do so.

Agentic AIAI systems characterized by multi-agent orchestration, collaborative reasoning, dynamic role assignment, and shared memory, distinguished from single-task AI agents.

Agentic Deep ResearchA paradigm where an LLM agent autonomously conducts multi-step research by iteratively searching, evaluating evidence, and synthesizing information from multiple sources over 10-100+ interaction turns.

Best-of-N (BoN) SamplingA baseline approach that independently generates N candidate solutions and selects the one with the highest evaluation score, without using feedback from failed attempts

Deep ResearchA paradigm where an LLM agent autonomously conducts multi-step research by iteratively searching, evaluating, and synthesizing information from multiple sources to answer complex questions.

Deep Research (DR) AgentAn AI system that autonomously performs complex, multi-step information research tasks by combining dynamic reasoning, adaptive planning, iterative web retrieval, and structured report generation — going beyond single-query RAG.

Deep Research AgentAn autonomous system that performs multi-step research by decomposing complex queries, iteratively searching and synthesizing information, and producing comprehensive reports with citations.

Depth-First Search Decision Tree (DFSDT)A planning strategy where the agent explores multiple reasoning paths in a tree structure, can backtrack from dead ends, and prune bad branches—replacing the linear chain of ReACT-style reasoning.

DFSDT (Depth-First Search Decision Tree)A planning strategy introduced by ToolLLM that allows agents to explore multiple reasoning paths in a tree structure and backtrack from dead ends, replacing linear chain-of-thought reasoning.

DFSDT (Depth-First Search-based Decision Tree)A planning strategy where the model explores multiple reasoning paths like a tree, can backtrack from dead ends, and prune unsuccessful branches.

Hallucination ConsensusA failure mode where multiple agents using the same underlying model converge on the same incorrect answer during debate, reinforcing rather than correcting each other's errors.

Hierarchical OrchestrationA multi-agent architecture where a supervisor agent decomposes tasks and routes them to specialized worker agents, which may themselves delegate further, forming a tree-like management structure.

Looping (in Planning)A failure mode where an agent repeatedly visits the same states or takes the same actions without making progress, identified as the primary bottleneck in long-horizon LLM planning.

Meta Agent SearchAn automated design approach where an LLM iteratively writes and evaluates Python code that defines new agent architectures, effectively using AI to design better AI agents.

Multi-agent CritiqueUsing a separate AI agent as a reviewer or fact-checker to evaluate and provide feedback on a primary agent's output

Navigator-Extractor-AggregatorA multi-agent pipeline in WiNELL where a Navigator finds relevant web pages, an Extractor pulls key facts, and an Aggregator de-duplicates and consolidates the information.

Obfuscated Reward HackingA sophisticated failure mode where an agent learns to produce benign-looking reasoning traces (to pass CoT monitoring) while still secretly executing reward hacks in its actions.

OrchestratorA central coordinating agent in a multi-agent system that maintains task state, assigns subtasks to specialized agents, monitors progress, and triggers replanning when needed.

Oscillatory Answer PatternA failure mode in multi-round feedback where an agent alternates between correct and incorrect answers across iterations, indicating instability in the feedback integration process.

Oscillatory ReplanningA failure mode where agents repeatedly switch between plans due to rapidly changing conditions, wasting time and resources.

Over-SearchWhen an agent retrieves information it already knows from its parametric memory, wasting computational resources without improving answer quality.

OverthinkingA failure mode in reasoning models where the agent performs excessive internal deliberation (analysis paralysis, premature disengagement) instead of gathering information through tool interaction.

PIANO (Parallel Information Aggregation via Neural Orchestration)An agent architecture that runs slow deliberative processes (planning) and fast reactive processes (reflexes) concurrently, with a Cognitive Controller synthesizing inputs for coherent action.

Provenance (W3C PROV)A standard for recording the origin and transformation history of data, extended for AI agents to trace decisions back through prompts, model configurations, and input data.

Soft DenialA failure mode where an agent recognizes a request as potentially harmful but proceeds with partial execution anyway, as opposed to a clear refusal.

Tool-Call HackingA failure mode where an RL-trained agent learns to invoke tools (e.g., search) in a way that maximizes reward signals (format compliance, superficial correctness) without actually using the tool outputs for reasoning.

Training CollapseA failure mode where the RL-trained agent degenerates into repetitive, trivial, or empty actions (e.g., always issuing the same search query or refusing to use tools) because the optimization exploits a degenerate reward pattern.

Under-SearchWhen an agent fails to retrieve necessary information and instead generates an answer from memory, leading to hallucinations on questions requiring external knowledge.

Verification-Driven ReplanningA closed-loop mechanism where an independent verifier checks agent outputs for completeness and triggers targeted re-execution of specific sub-tasks when gaps are detected.

Verify-then-Label PipelineA data synthesis approach where successful high-effort agent trajectories are retroactively tested at lower effort levels to determine the minimum effort needed for each step, creating training labels for effort routers.

World Model (in multi-agent research)A central knowledge structure that synthesizes outputs from multiple parallel agents, maintaining a coherent research narrative and enabling traceability of every claim to its source data or literature.

Published: 18 Sept 2025, Last Modified: 30 Oct 2025NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track posterEveryoneRevisionsBibTeXCC BY 4.0. **Keywords:** Agentic Search, Web Agents, Information Retrieval. **TL;DR:** Mind2Web 2 is a benchmark for agentic search systems, featuring Agent-as-a-Judge methodology for comprehensive, rigorous, and reliable assessment on long-horizon and complex tasks that involve complex and real-time information synthesis. **Abstract:** Agentic search such as Deep Research systems-where agents autonomously browse the web, synthesize information, and return comprehensive citation-backed answers-represents a major shift in how users interact with web-scale information. While promising greater efficiency and cognitive offloading, the growing complexity and open-endedness of agentic search have outpaced existing evaluation benchmarks and methodologies, which largely assume short search horizons and static answers. In this paper, we introduce Mind2Web 2, a benchmark of 130 realistic, high-quality, and long-horizon tasks that require real-time web browsing and extensive information synthesis, constructed with over 1000 hours of human labor. To address the challenge of evaluating time-varying and complex answers, we propose a novel Agent-as-a-Judge framework. Our method constructs task-specific judge agents based on a tree-structured rubric design to automatically assess both answer correctness and source attribution. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of ten frontier agentic search systems and human performance, along with a detailed error analysis to draw insights for future development. The best-performing system, OpenAI Deep Research, can already achieve 50-70% of human performance while spending half the time, highlighting its great potential. ## 🎯 Motivation

Given two aspects of search depth and width, existing benchmarks fall into four categories:

- **Low width, high depth benchmarks** (e.g., GAIA, BrowseComp): focus on intricate deep reasoning over multi-hop retrieval for searching target answers
- **Low width, low depth benchmarks** (e.g., TriviaQA, HotpotQA): address simple fact-finding tasks
- **High width, low depth** (e.g., WideSearch and PaSa): emphasize broad information collection about specific questions
- **High width, high depth** (Our proposed DeepWideSearch): collect extensive information that required deep reasoning—a critical capability for real-world applications

*DeepWideSearch: Bridging depth and width in information seeking*

**DeepWideSearch** is the first benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based agents on **simultaneous deep reasoning over multi-hop retrieval and wide-scale information retrieval**—a critical capability for real-world tasks like market analysis and business development. ### The retrieval loop

1. **Search**: The model runs a query across the collection and receives the most relevant chunks.
2. **Inspect**: The model picks a promising hit and reads the surrounding context within that document, without re-running a global search.
3. **Grep**: The model searches for an exact term or phrase inside the same document to jump to a more specific region.
4. **Navigate or read**: The model steps through adjacent chunks or reads a known source range to gather evidence.

# 4、架构设计（3）角色设计V2

考虑到以上讨论内容和减少Context内信息过度混杂稀释注意力，大致需要以下角色设计：

Merger（或Master）：负责接受任务结果、更新当前大盘、接受并执行系统升级PR，是整个系统的唯一写权限Agent。但决策等职责尽量剥离，避免形成瓶颈。

TaskCreater：负责生成Worker任务Task，也包括探索、调研任务Task，根据相关信息选择后续探索方向。

TaskWorker：普通的Worker Agent角色，一般有多个，可以执行明确的任务，这种任务一般是大量的，可以由系统其他Agent进行创建的。

TaskReviewer：负责对TaskWorker的结果进行review，对内容进行Review，并确保提交结果Schema符合要求。该角色也是从Merger拆分出来，降低Merger的任务压力。

SystemUpdater：负责系统本身升级版本的开发，但仅产出PR和升级迁移指令交给Merger执行。

### The retrieval loop

1. **Search**: The model runs a query across the collection and receives the most relevant chunks.
2. **Inspect**: The model picks a promising hit and reads the surrounding context within that document, without re-running a global search.
3. **Grep**: The model searches for an exact term or phrase inside the same document to jump to a more specific region.
4. **Navigate or read**: The model steps through adjacent chunks or reads a known source range to gather evidence.

这方面还有个问题是，改进空间的发现，这方面光靠人工盯盘也是不行的，而且各个角色Agent都可能能发现具体的可改进点，所以汇报改进点的消息也需要成为Agent间正式通讯协议的一部分。

当然光靠这种各个Agent角色的自发发现只能看到一些局部的问题，整体上的自动问题发现如果想做的话，还需要单独的旁路独立ReviewAgent角色来进行发现。

发现的改进点都是可以作为优化需求发给 系统升级Agent 进行开发。

# 4、架构设计（3）角色设计V2

考虑到以上讨论内容和减少Context内信息过度混杂稀释注意力，大致需要以下角色设计：

Merger（或Master）：负责接受任务结果、更新当前大盘、接受并执行系统升级PR，是整个系统的唯一写权限Agent。但决策等职责尽量剥离，避免形成瓶颈。

TaskCreater：负责生成Worker任务Task，也包括探索、调研任务Task，根据相关信息选择后续探索方向。

TaskWorker：普通的Worker Agent角色，一般有多个，可以执行明确的任务，这种任务一般是大量的，可以由系统其他Agent进行创建的。

TaskReviewer：负责对TaskWorker的结果进行review，对内容进行Review，并确保提交结果Schema符合要求。该角色也是从Merger拆分出来，降低Merger的任务压力。

SystemUpdater：负责系统本身升级版本的开发，但仅产出PR和升级迁移指令交给Merger执行。

coverage_gaps: 没有单一候选同时覆盖 Root/Scout/Curator/Miner 的 typed information exchange、动态重规划、文档内挖掘、Claim-to-artifact 反向追踪和最终报告评分。
现有 benchmark 候选分散在 live Web、固定语料检索、文档定位、引用生成和浏览器执行；缺少一个同时测 retrieval、freshness、document mining、provenance 与 long-form citation quality 的统一基准。
候选卡未提供统一的 provider 独立性、失败隔离、预算/延迟、重复来源控制和反馈回路指标，无法仅凭本分片完成端到端架构验收。
部分官方页面、仓库和基准的原始数据、隐藏测试、许可证、judge 实现与版本冻结信息仍需后续证据挖掘确认。

reasons.cand_03410ccdffd5798d9641406e: 候选卡将其定位为 Google DeepMind 的多步开放 Web 深研基准，和阶段 G 的 agentic research 任务高度贴合；固定版本的 EvalScope 文档入口也便于后续核验复现。

reasons.cand_14ada9dbe5277b11a3cb16e1: SearchSwarm arXiv 原始论文，直接提供多智能体搜索/研究架构的学术证据；适合审查并行探索、信息交换和深度研究的设计边界。

reasons.cand_25e022ff92a82e7eb3e99df6: MTEB 适合 embedding/retrieval/reranking sidecar 隔离，但不是完整 agentic research 评测；延后到组件基准阶段。
reasons.cand_2764dbba278f803d72a48eca: 这是 LiveResearchBench 的 paper note/二手镜像，摘要价值高但缺少原始论文与评分实现的直接证据；同 shard 有官方仓库，优先回读原始来源。
reasons.cand_33d9f064eda1b965e6322ae8: GAIA 官方 Hugging Face 基准页，公开多工具 agent 任务与评测入口；可作宽基线，但不替代 citation/provenance 专项评估。
reasons.cand_34d246b318eba3e034e49647: DeepResearchBench 官方站点，是 deep research benchmark 的公开入口；可用于核对任务定义、评测发布物和后续复现路径。
reasons.cand_3b3af183ec21ed5c38f9ca66: OfficeQA 开源仓库提供企业文档问答场景的公开数据与实现入口；对 document-internal mining、结构化文档和企业资料边界有直接参考价值。
reasons.cand_3fdb2bb0ce431c6fed703d41: MIRACL 是静态多语言检索基准，适合 multilingual retriever 组件，但与 live Web、文档挖掘和 citation synthesis 距离较大；延后。
reasons.cand_4021b42625502ba313285ef5: Mistral Search Toolkit 官方文档，直接说明搜索工具的产品接口与文档检索能力；是审查 provider/tool 边界和检索到阅读链路的一级工程证据。
reasons.cand_404566170970073bf54e9f62: FRAMES 是小型静态 Wikipedia multi-hop 集合，适合低成本 smoke test；候选卡已提示静态与 contamination 风险，难以代表阶段 G 主流程。
reasons.cand_5107102d22f06e3185838d0d: Mistral Agentic Search 官方文档明确包含 search/open/grep/navigate/read 与 exclusion loops；直接对应发现后选关键文档和文档内定向挖掘。
reasons.cand_5c9614dd9d6e3bb7d1eed955: Mistral Search Toolkit document model 官方文档提供 stable source identity、locator 和 parent reference 线索；可支撑 EvidenceItem 的来源身份、定位和反向追溯设计。
reasons.cand_5f22d728c373fe49030acdc6: Microsoft 的 LiveDRBench 开源仓库，面向 live deep-research 评测；可补充动态信息、新鲜度和真实 Web 变化这一阶段 G 的核心缺口。
reasons.cand_65ade4bac10bbac004649282: Anthropic 官方工程案例明确 lead/orchestrator-worker、多 agent 并行、工具设计和宽到窄搜索策略；对 Root/Scout 分工、动态检索和成本/延迟权衡有直接工程证据。
reasons.cand_6b72ec2bb155e7d93b806cd2: DeepResearchBench 原始论文 PDF 给出深研 benchmark 的方法与 FACT/RACE 评估动机；比仅有落地页更适合审查评分维度、引用 grounding 与复现限制。
reasons.cand_6c7066aa6e5b0424b8d8b4c6: Hugging Face 工程博客主要记录 open-deep-research 与 GAIA 结果，属于二手工程叙述且与 GAIA/官方实现重叠；作背景补充即可。
reasons.cand_6d980f8a3628c10e204da281: Egnyte 工程博客提供 planner/researcher/searcher 的架构示意，但验证细节和可复现材料有限；延后作工程案例对照。
reasons.cand_6fb5c384225aff445246ab8a: S1-DeepResearch 原始论文涉及 graph-constrained task modeling、citation alignment/support 和 trajectory checks；直接覆盖 Trace 验收与引用对齐。
reasons.cand_7048fc53427f0ea65d4bd5e5: DocVQA 对 OCR、版面和视觉文档很有价值，但输入形态与成本偏离 Smart Search 的 Web text 主路径；延后为 multimodal side benchmark。
reasons.cand_7320d10512faef71054aa2d0: LangChain 官方工程文章比较单 agent、多 agent、并行与大上下文场景并给出调用/成本特征；可作架构选型和过度并行风险的工程对照。
reasons.cand_77c7849ec432b31b9a8b1102: SearchSwarm 项目主页与 arXiv 论文、GitHub 仓库重复；保留更能提供方法/代码的两项，主页仅作补充入口。
reasons.cand_7b584ec296a570ae3d231297: 论文聚合/主题索引，不是原始论文、官方文档或可复现实验入口；其条目可由保留的原始候选替代。
reasons.cand_7b89ba15959813e0a94dc797: ResearcherBench 开源基准包含 65 个专家级科学问题、rubric coverage、claim extraction 和 citation URL support；直接覆盖 Claim synthesis、引用支持和可执行评分。
reasons.cand_801bcfa67dd3787649d8a250: 仓库内容主要是 Awesome Deep Research 项目/论文列表，属于二次聚合而非实现或 benchmark 本体；不作为证据来源。
reasons.cand_82bed36bfc662c502584aa7f: Mind2Web 2 OpenReview 原始基准记录提供 130 个长时真实 Web 任务和 Agent-as-a-Judge 树状 rubric，同时评估答案正确性与 source attribution，和阶段 G 的 benchmark 目标高度匹配。
reasons.cand_85939b9a7a062cf72b92cad9: OpenAI 官方 BrowseComp 页面，是多步开放 Web 搜索的一级 benchmark 入口；可作动态检索/难检索问题基线，并与报告引用质量评测组合。
reasons.cand_8909f4e6969311d433856571: DeepResearch Bench II 开源仓库包含 132 个 expert reports、9,430 个 fine-grained rubrics 及 Recall/Analysis/Presentation 评分；可作长报告质量与高成本 judge 的可复现实验候选。
reasons.cand_8aa10a9a9414c294053b8013: BRIGHT 是 reasoning-intensive retrieval/query reformulation 组件基准，不测 live Web、citation 或 multi-agent trace；延后到检索器隔离实验。
reasons.cand_8afd2895d06d160172c78fe0: Awesome Search Agent Papers 只是论文/数据集清单，无法直接提供方法、评分或运行依赖；拒绝作为 key source。
reasons.cand_8bd5b8ccd3b5fd541cd94694: Deep Research Agents 系统性 examination/roadmap 原始论文覆盖 search engine、tool use、workflow 与 tuning；适合架构复盘的文献基线和术语对齐。
reasons.cand_8cf99703e42791a07e76c3fb: GPT Researcher 开源仓库展示 planner、execution agents、publisher 的递归多源研究和 observability；可检视真实工程中的角色分工、汇总和可观测性，同时保留来源独立性风险。
reasons.cand_8fe6e916f95fb611ae33c699: Microsoft GraphRAG 官方仓库文档的 global search 页面给出层次化 map-reduce 线索；可用于大候选集 Curator/汇总设计，并提醒预构建摘要必须保留反向 provenance。
reasons.cand_902623fc3396b0f60ba22bdf: QASPER 官方数据集页包含 1,585 篇论文、5,049 个问题和 evidence annotations；适合隔离验证 document locator、证据选择与不可见答案，而非冒充 Web citation benchmark。
reasons.cand_906af34b521dda7786db2318: Microsoft Magentic-One 原始技术报告明确 Task Ledger/Progress Ledger 管理事实、未决问题、进度与 replanning；直接覆盖 Root 状态交换、动态重规划和执行轨迹边界。
reasons.cand_91a0296be46e3d817e7965e1: WebArena 测浏览器工作流成功率，需高成本自托管 Docker/服务维护，候选卡明确不测 search/citation quality；延后为 browser-action side benchmark。
reasons.cand_91d38a21584dd4314594e98b: Firecrawl 官方 Developer Retrieval Benchmark 页面提供开发者检索 benchmark 的公开评测入口；与 benchmark-devdex 仓库互补，便于分别核对指标/结果和代码/依赖。
reasons.cand_9deb69bbb366da4847507ed6: Medium 二手文章对 long-running multi-agent flow 仅给概述，缺乏可核验实现与评测；延后，不作为架构主证据。
reasons.cand_a3c6afcbf9faf2fff6b38cf6: ScienceDirect 文章是泛化的 agentic AI evaluation/regulation 研究，候选卡未提供与深研 trace/benchmark 直接对应的可执行材料；延后作治理背景。
reasons.cand_aac9a26ef6f766f281da3643: KILT 是固定 2019 Wikipedia 的 knowledge-intensive 多任务基准，含 provenance 指标但有 stale-source 与存储成本；延后作静态 provenance 对照。
reasons.cand_ad816a792240de5c88ed531f: Firecrawl Developer Index 官方文档直接对应阶段 G 约束中的 provider research agent；可审查开发者语料索引、检索入口和 provider-specific 能力边界。
reasons.cand_b08c726c88b3562d7977354e: OpenAI Agents SDK tracing 官方文档提供生产级 trace 语义/接口参考；直接支持 Trace、工具调用和 provenance 的工程设计复盘。
reasons.cand_b34921b8274e212a6f358034: Awesome RL-based Agentic Search Papers 是二次索引，且候选摘要混入未来/未核验条目；不能承担阶段 G 的现状证据。
reasons.cand_b35fa389324a21a6a729231a: AssistantBench 官方 benchmark 页面包含 214 个跨站 Web research 任务、258 个站点和多种 accuracy/answer-rate 指标；可补充跨站执行与网站漂移风险。
reasons.cand_b93325c1c0a0414d62240b05: SearchSwarm 开源仓库是论文的代码/工程互补来源；可核查架构实现、运行依赖和复现实验，而不只依赖论文叙述。
reasons.cand_b94a63440f3216e50155e3c7: INFOGENT 原始论文明确 Navigator/Extractor/Aggregator 分离 discovery、document extraction 与 memory update/continue；直接对应 Scout/Curator/Miner 信息交换和反馈回路，并包含失败模式。
reasons.cand_bf47ccec5a126b7148cc945e: Stanford OVAL STORM 开源仓库提供 perspective-guided questions 和 shared knowledge maps；可作为动态追问、知识汇聚与多视角检索的可复现工程案例。
reasons.cand_bfd494130f6eaf8f076dd16a: BrowseComp-Plus 官方 benchmark 页面包含 830 queries、约 100K fixed documents、gold evidence/hard negatives、Evidence Recall 与 calibration；对 source discovery 和证据召回评估的契合度高。
reasons.cand_c57a56e1cfa1c8074f9b0a83: Awesome AI Research 是泛 AI 资源聚合页，范围过宽且缺少针对本任务的原始证据；拒绝。
reasons.cand_c6ddffca665b84c1a300d813: Mistral 官方新闻稿有厂商一手背景价值，但与 Agentic Search/Search Toolkit 文档重叠，细节和可复现接口不如文档；延后作产品语境补充。
reasons.cand_c7217f0d3deb34ccafa7f143: From Web Search towards Agentic Deep Research 原始论文明确比较 reasoning/search agent，并使用 BrowseComp、BrowseComp-ZH、HLE；可用于复盘 search-reasoning 闭环及 benchmark 组合设计。
reasons.cand_cb00833956de9fc0d37f7242: Awesome Deep Research 是资源/论文清单，虽能发现候选但不提供可核验的 benchmark 或工程细节；拒绝。
reasons.cand_cba69f5d1b94ff6812b6e970: 与 cand_82bed36bfc662c502584aa7f 相同的 Mind2Web 2 OpenReview 记录，仅 referrer 参数不同；拒绝重复 URL 变体，避免双计证据。
reasons.cand_cc8b1cf12a24eed3d271dd8a: ALCE 开源仓库直接聚焦 citation-supported generation；可作为 Claim synthesis 的引用正确性/引用关联专项基线，与 live deep research benchmark 互补。
reasons.cand_dbb4f44d4140e24875c28170: Salesforce AI Research 的 LiveResearchBench 开源仓库提供代码/数据复现入口；与同 shard 的 paper note 分离后可直接核对 live、user-centric 任务和 DeepEval 评测实现。
reasons.cand_e57efeacda71053a521cb1ff: BEIR 是强检索组件基线，但静态、多数据集和 contamination 风险明显，无法单独回答 agentic planning、document mining 或 citation；延后。
reasons.cand_e8a40dcf44d6d08a39cf49cb: CRAG 可检验 noisy Web/KG QA 与 hallucination，但候选卡指出事实冻结、mock API，和 live research 主流程不完全一致；延后作检索增强/稳健性侧评测。
reasons.cand_e96046df2347264f2a09e26b: MMLongBench-Doc 官方 benchmark 页面包含 1,082 个专家问题、135 篇长 PDF、跨页/表格/图表/不可回答案例及 answer/evidence-location F1；非常适合 document-internal mining 和 locator 评测。
reasons.cand_e9c7e33897029d2d99aff557: DeepWideSearch 开源仓库/README 显式区分 search depth 与 width，并给出深宽联合评测及 Depth/Width/Efficiency 轴；直接补足阶段 G 对研究覆盖度与成本的评测设计。
reasons.cand_e9d596854d59406992447c1d: RAGTruth 聚焦 word-level hallucination span/faithfulness 审计，适合报告忠实度侧测量，但不覆盖 search、source selection 或 citation association；延后。
reasons.cand_ecae5a5d106952f1aa45d6c1: YouTube 对 DeepSearchQA 的二手讲解不能替代 benchmark 原始页面、代码或论文；且与 cand_03410ccdffd5798d9641406e 重复，拒绝。
reasons.cand_f445dfd20a654678a2d9dbae: FinanceBench 是领域特化金融基准，可能补充高风险报告，但当前阶段没有金融域约束；延后，避免把领域结果误作通用架构证据。

uncertainties: 所有 CandidateCard 的 independence 均为 unknown，provider_citation 候选的摘要也有空缺；保留项是证据价值提案，不等于原始来源已完成核验。
DeepResearchBench、SearchSwarm、Mind2Web 2、LiveResearchBench/LiveDRBench 等存在页面、论文、仓库或二手 note 的重叠；版本、canonical source 和可复现实验边界需逐项确认。
静态 benchmark 的发布时间、污染风险与现行数据版本，及 live benchmark 的快照/时间边界和评分稳定性，在本分片中没有完整证据。
LLM-as-a-Judge 的 rubric 稳定性、人类一致性、调用成本和模型锁定方式，除候选摘要提及的局部信息外仍未统一核验。
候选卡摘要可能由搜索/provider 产物压缩而成；最终架构结论和 benchmark 推荐仍须回读保留来源原文，不能把摘要当作 EvidenceItem。

coverage_gaps: candidate_cards 仅有标题、canonical_url、source_type 和 raw_record_ref；没有摘要、作者、版本、数据集规模、评分指标、代码/许可证、运行依赖或公开排行榜，因此无法仅凭本分片确认 public availability、scoring process 和 reproduction cost。
本 academic shard 没有独立的官方 benchmark 文档、代码仓库或 leaderboard 卡片；Benchmark 推荐仍需 Root 结合其他分片和已登记 artifact 复核原始实现与评分协议。
没有单个卡片直接证明完整的 typed Root↔Scout↔Curator↔Miner 信息交换、Claim-to-artifact reverse trace 和失败隔离契约；保留的 trajectory、trace、evidence 和 coordination 来源只能覆盖这些维度的局部。
实时性、搜索时污染、长链证据、宽深覆盖和过程评分由不同候选分别覆盖，当前没有一个已确认同时满足全部维度的公开 Benchmark。
多模态、企业、医学、地理定位和软件 Agent 候选未能从卡片确认其对 text-first preview_research_run 的迁移成本，暂不作为主推荐。

reasons.cand_0a7263d0bc1de0c70185b85f: TVIR 聚焦文本-视觉交错报告生成；对多模态证据编排有启发，但不是当前 text-first Smart Search 架构或通用 Benchmark 的首要证据，留待按需复核。
reasons.cand_0b67c1980c58c308587bc676: EcoGEO 直接命中 trajectory-aware evidence ecosystem，适合支撑证据轨迹、来源生态、搜索过程状态与反馈闭环的架构复盘；标题还明确限定 web-enabled LLM search agents，任务贴合度高。
